title: Horizontal boundary term of signed localized Koszul evaluation
statement: Let A be a commutative ring, f:Fin(r)→A, F an arbitrary complex of module sheaves on Spec(A) [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], e a natural number, I the extended negative Koszul tail at exponent e+1 [def-sc-koszul-open-system], and z a degree n Hom cochain into global sections of F [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. Assume |J|>1 for the component being calculated. Let B_J be the transported increasing wedge for every nonempty J. Put p=|J|-1, q=n+1-p and S(p,m)=p*(m-p)+p*(p-1)/2. Signed restriction and division by prod(J)^(e+1) of ((n+1).negOnePow • d_I^(−p) followed by z^(1−p))(B_J), with sign (-1)^S(p,n+1), equals the alternating sum over j in J of signed localized evaluation of z on B_(J.erase j), restricted to D(prod(J)) and transported to F^q. The deletion sign is (-1) to the number of elements of J smaller than j. Empty erased subsets contribute zero [def-sc-principal-open-alternating-total]. This is only the precomposition term: it has no coefficient differential.

source.place: Stacks Project Tags 08D0 and 08D1, read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08D0 and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08D1; fraction differential calculation and coefficient naturality with totalization signs.

proof.text: For |J|>1, both tail terms are supported and every erased subset is nonempty. Transport the negative boundary to the exterior-power term. Contraction of the increasing wedge is the negative sum of the wedges with one generator deleted, with coefficient (-1)^position*f(j)^(e+1); increasing enumeration identifies position with the number of elements smaller than j.

Apply z and restriction to the sum, using A-linearity. Factor prod(J)=f(j)*prod(J.erase j). All factors are invertible on D(prod(J)). To prove the denominator cancellation identity, apply the injective scalar multiplication by prod(J)^(e+1) to both proposed fractions: the inverse equations and A-linearity of restriction identify both with f(j)^(e+1) times the original restricted numerator. Functoriality composes the restrictions.

Use principalCech_erase_degree for the coefficient-degree transport. The negative boundary together with (n+1).negOnePow leaves n.negOnePow. For p>0, S(p,n+1)+n-S(p-1,n) is even: its integer expression is 2*n-2*p+2. Thus the remaining sign is exactly the deletion sign times the erased evaluation sign. Equality term by term yields the sum. Empty opens have zero sections and require no cancellation in A.
